content.title: Venezuela beats USA to win 2026 World Baseball Classic championship: Live updates and reaction
content.text: Venezuela won its first WBC title behind stellar pitching that held USA’s star-studded lineup to just three hitsVenezuela celebrates winning the WBC for the first time Getty ImagesVenezuela beats USA in WBC finalVenezuela has won the World Baseball Classic for the first time, upsetting a star-studded United States team 3-2 in the championship game in Miami. Venezuela jumped out to a 2-0 lead thanks to a Maikel García sacrifice fly and a Wilyer Abreu home run. Team USA’s offense was lifeless, recording just two hits over the first seven innings, before Bryce Harper tied the game with a booming two-run homer in the eighth. The Venezuelans quickly retook the lead in the top of the ninth however, thanks to a Eugenio Suárez RBI double, before Daniel Palencia closed out the game. This is the second straight time the U.S. has finished as WBC runners-up after losing to Japan in the 2023 final. Share your reaction with us at live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty ImagesAs for the scenes in the locker room …New MLB season just around the corner!What a tournament! Eight days until Opening Day …Lopez and his coaching staff Evan Drellich / The AthleticVenezuela manager Omar López brought his entire coaching staff with him to his postgame press conference. That includes former MLB stars like Johan Santana (sitting directly to Lopez’s left on the dais), Victor Martinez (wearing the hat standing behind Santana) and Miguel Cabrera (bottom left corner, looking at the camera).A sweet celebration still unfolding in Miami The Athletic / Kaci BorowskiThe game ended almost two hours ago, but Venezuela players and their families are still out on the field, taking turns for a photo op with the WBC trophy in the dugout and playing games of tag on the outfield grass. It’s a really peaceful and lovely contrast inside what has been an incredibly boisterous house this week.Perez adds to his resumeSalvador Perez joked after Venezuela’s win that he can “retire now” after winning the World Baseball Classic. Whenever the Venezuela and Royals team captain does retire, he will do so with an unimpeachable career resume — as the Royals highlighted on social media.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPerez on support from Venezuela Imagn ImagesSalvador Perez was asked in his postgame press conference to share a message with Venezuelans. This was his response:💬 “Just today, after beating Italy (in the semifinal), I saw the videos of the people on the streets celebrating in the smallest town in the country, a black and white TV set, and those people supporting us, kneeling down.“They were with us here in our hearts. I would like to thank them from the bottom of my heart. Thank you for the support. Thank you for the positive messages we all received.“And even the not very positive messages, those messages motivated us as well, and I have to thank for that too. Those that judged us when we struck out, people that spoke so many bad things about us — that motivated us as well.”Respect between Team USA, VenezuelaBryce Harper congratulated several Venezuela players on winning the World Baseball Classic, including Ronald Acuña Jr., after the game was over.Bobby Witt Jr. also shared a moment with Royals teammate Salvador Perez.Delcy Rodríguez, the acting president of Venezuela, has decreed that tomorrow will be a national holiday so Venezuelans can celebrate their team’s World Baseball Classic triumph.He decidido decretar mañana como Día de Júbilo Nacional, no laborable, con excepción de los trabajadores de servicios esenciales, para que nuestra juventud salga a las plazas, a los parques y a las canchas a festejar.¡Mañana todos al gran concierto Venezuela triunfa unida!— Delcy Rodríguez (@delcyrodriguezv) March 18, 2026 Suárez’s MLB manager on his heroics Cincinnati Reds manager Terry Francona beamed Tuesday night when Eugenio Suárez’s name was brought up following his team’s Cactus League game against the Cleveland Guardians.Because he was managing, all Francona knew was that Suárez had a big hit and Venezuela won. Francona said …💬 “We might not get him back, they may be going to Venezuela.” Francona has been supportive of players playing in the WBC, but he also worried about players missing time and not getting the number of at-bats they’d normally get in spring. Suárez has played five Cactus League games and five WBC games for Venezuela, with 15 plate appearances for the Reds and 21 for Venezuela. Last season Suárez had 62 plate appearances in spring for the Arizona Diamondbacks. Francona added …💬 “He’s gotten shorted at-bats from what he’s got normally, but he’s also got at-bats in stadiums with 50,000, so you hope the tradeoff works.” Suárez was just 4 for 20 in the WBC, but in addition to his championship-winning double, he also had a pair of home runs. Francona continued …💬 “It’s hard when you don’t have your guys here, but it’s good for baseball. It sounded like the atmosphere was great. That’s good. That’s really, really good.”And now the WBC hero will return to the Reds this week.💬 “That’s even better.”What went wrong for Team USA? Getty ImagesTeam USA manager Mark DeRosa admitted the U.S. offense fell well short of expectations, and also said the tournament format might change in the future to a point when more players are in more midseason form. Speaking to reporters postgame, DeRosa said …💬 “I’m not going to make excuses … it’s early in spring training, guys are getting ready for the season. Eventually the tournament gets moved and the guys are in better form pitching-wise.“But ultimately it’s who gets hot at the right time, who gets a big swing. It just seemed like we couldn’t get the offense going the entire tournament.“We came out of Arizona absolutely smoking the ball in the two exhibition games we played and for what whatever reason, we just couldn’t get it rolling offensively. Even tonight, you look up in the seventh, and they had a two-hit shutout.“Hats off to them. For them to battle last night against Italy, for them to use their entire bullpen, those guys to come back out on no rest was pretty special to watch.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDeRosa on managing Team USA again: ‘100 percent yes’Mark DeRosa has now led Team USA to back-to-back World Baseball Classic finals — and back-to-back losses. DeRosa also took a lot of criticism for misspeaking ahead of the U.S. loss to Italy, when he implied on MLB Network he thought his team had already clinched a spot to advance out of pool play when it had not. So given all that, would DeRosa want to manage Team USA in a third WBC? Here’s what he said, per our Evan Drellich…💬 “It would be 100 percent yes to do it again. Love to get over the finish line ... Why? If you saw how hurting the guys are in the locker room now, you’d know why.”More from DeRosa Getty ImagesMark DeRosa said he would have only put Mason Miller into the game if the U.S. had the lead.DeRosa sentimental about Harper Getty ImagesTeam USA manager Mark DeRosa and tonight’s would-be U.S. hero Bryce Harper go back a long way. Here’s what the manager had to say about it …💬 “I’ve known Bryce for a long time. I was with the Nationals in 2012 when he was 19 years old and came to his first big league camp and spent a lot of time with him, we have a lot of history and I wanted him to be a part of this. “I knew he was going to have a moment, that’s who he is. He has the ability to have big moments in big spots. He wants it. He wants to be up there in that spot. “Yeah, it hurts. We shared a special moment in my office after the game. I watched him grow up in the game. Lot of conversations, knew what his career was going to be like with the multiple MVPs, and how he’s competed. I was just proud he was a part of the team. Just to get to spend two and a half weeks, share a clubhouse with him again.”Brotherly loveWilliam and Willson Contreras have both spent several seasons in Major League Baseball, but never on the same team. You can see the emotions pouring out when the two got to celebrate winning the World Baseball Classic together on Team Venezuela!Perez chokes back tears Getty ImagesSalvador Pérez was as emotional as anyone, sitting down with the Fox Sports crew as Venezuela’s on-field celebrations finally started to settled down. He started with his feelings and a joke …💬 “It’s unbelievable. I’m super happy. And now I feel like I can retire! I know a lot of people didn’t believe in this team but we did it. We did it and we’re number one.”Then when it came to describing what it all means back home in Venezuela, it was more of a choke back of tears … 💬 “Oh my God. I’m gonna be honest with you guys, and there’s nothing that I can hide, you know? All you guys see, what happened, all that … and ... I know people are super happy right now in my country. Sorry, I’m sorry …“Where I come from, all my family, it’s hard to get to see me play in the big league. I got some family that never had that opportunity. So now they’ve seen me play. I know they’re super happy and me as well, for my family and for other people from Venezuela.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBrutal deja-vu for USATeam USA lost the 2023 World Baseball Classic final 3-2 to Japan.Three years later, with an even better roster, Team USA lost the 2026 World Baseball Classic final to Venezuela by the same score.More disappointment for Judge, Harper Getty ImagesAaron Judge and Bryce Harper have a claim to be considered the two best MLB players currently active who have never won a World Series. A World Baseball Classic title is not the same, but it would have given the two superstars something as they continue to chase a World Series title into their thirties.Instead, more questions will follow about their ability to produce in big moments — even after Harper’s clutch game-tying home run tonight.List of World Baseball Classic champions Getty ImagesTeam USA’s loss tonight means Japan is still the only multi-time World Baseball Classic winner — and Venezuela’s win means that four different countries have now won the tournament.
